treaty_name: Convention between the Republic of India and the State of Israel for the avoidance of double taxation and for the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and on capital (1996, as amended by Protocol 2015; modified by MLI)
eif_quote: Whereas the annexed Convention between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the State of Israel for the avoidance of double taxation and for the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and on capital has entered into force on the 15th May, 1996 ... Notification : No. GSR 256(E), dated 26-6-1996.
source_title: Income Tax Department of India (law.incometaxindia.gov.in) - Notification GSR 256(E) and annexed India-Israel Convention, Wayback copy of 29 Oct 2011; amending Protocol (Hebrew) from gov.il, Wayback copy

However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the dividends the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

2. However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the interest the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

2. However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the royalties, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: 1. Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement.

notes: Effect (Art. 29(2)): WHT on dividends, interest, royalties and FTS for amounts paid or credited on or after the first day of the month following entry into force (15 May 1996) in both States, i.e. 1 June 1996. Fees for technical services: separate Art. 13 (not modelled). Interest on government bonds and on loans/credits made, refinanced, guaranteed or insured by the Reserve Bank of India, Bank of Israel and other listed institutions is taxable only in the residence State (Art. 11(3)) - not modelled. MFN: the 1996 Protocol para 2 contained an MFN clause (rate or scope lower than in this Convention under any Indian treaty with a third State entering into force after 1-1-1995 to apply automatically). The amending Protocol signed 14-10-2015 (in force 19-12-2016 per both MLI lists) Article 5 deletes paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Protocol ('ס"ק 2 ו-3 לפרוטוקול מושמטים'), effective in India for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 April following its entry into force and in Israel for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January following - so no MFN applies today; no Indian notification of an MFN reduction was found for earlier periods either. The 2015 Protocol also replaces Art. 13(4) (capital gains), deletes Art. 24(3)-(4), replaces Art. 27 (exchange of information) and inserts Art. 27A (limitation of benefits: main-purpose test, domestic anti-avoidance, beneficial ownership); Arts 10-12 were not amended (read from the Hebrew text of the Protocol, gov.il, via Wayback; English text not obtained). MLI: Art. 7(1) PPT applies (India notified Art. 27A(1) as an existing Art. 7(2) provision). MLI WHT effect 2020-01-01 per map.json; Indian side from 1 April 2020 (India chose Art. 35(2) 'taxable period'). India's SLOB choice not verified for Israel - PPT only.
